PullRequest.Title: Sweeper skills v7: split sweeper-fix into sweeper-plan and sweeper-implement
PullRequest.Body:
**TL;DR:** the vcodesweeper has now support for both **implementing** and **planning** an implementation for a reviewed issue. The PR adds the corresponding skills.

Replaces `.github/skills/sweeper-fix` (v6, #336827) with two skills.

**`sweeper-plan <n>`** — for a *plan first* agent-ready record, asks the review's open decisions in chat, writes `.sweeper/plans/issue-<n>.md` (git-excluded via `.git/info/exclude`, never committed). It writes no code; the maintainer edits the plan in their editor.

**`sweeper-implement <n>`** — implements. On an *implement* record it works straight from the review's brief; on a *plan first* record it reads the plan file as the maintainer left it. Tests are written first (fail before, pass after), the diff is validated against the brief or plan. After the maintainer's go-ahead it opens a **draft PR** under their identity, via `--body-file`, and keeps it a draft.

Tested end to end on the sweeper sandbox in VS Code chat and in the Agents window (plan-first and implement, plus the plan-record-without-a-plan refusal) before this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a plan for a plan-first Sweeper issue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sequential checkout/auth preconditions, review-record fetch, live issue fetch, open-PR search, any required reproduction, and local plan/exclude-file write must complete before the maintainer receives the plan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git remote/status and resolve the repository exclude path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant three local git invocations per plan request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted combined sweeper-fix skill performed the same checkout/status checks and wrote the same excluded plan file; the new skill adds worktree-safe path resolution rather than a new repeated scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preconditions and exclude-path resolution block plan creation but do not scale with source-tree size beyond git status's normal tracked-worktree scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate GitHub CLI, fetch one Sweeper record, fetch one live issue, and search open PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One auth check, one record request, one issue request, and one PR search per invocation; no per-file or per-record fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted combined skill had the same initial auth, record, live-issue, and open-PR checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These sequential requests gate plan creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update git's exclude file if needed and write one issue plan file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two small file writes per planned issue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The combined skill also updated an exclude file and wrote one plan file; the new path resolution supports linked worktrees without increasing write cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to hand the editable plan to the maintainer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested issue; source reproduction may depend on that issue, but the added workflow itself has constant cardinality and no collection-sized loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The prescribed gates are sequential; there is no concurrency burst or unbounded queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. The workflow intentionally fetches live issue/PR state rather than caching it; the plan file persists locally for the implementation handoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete skill diff and explicit command sequence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub and test latency varies, but no changed scaling mechanism is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this extracts pre-existing plan work into a dedicated skill without adding scaling work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Implement an implement-ready issue directly from its Sweeper brief and open a draft PR
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sequential preconditions and GitHub gates precede code/test work; validation and maintainer review precede refreshed live gates, push, and PR creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate, fetch one record and live issue, search open PRs, then later refresh live issue/PR gates, push one branch, and create one draft PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant requests per issue plus one push and one PR creation; no per-changed-file network call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The combined skill prescribed the same initial gates, refreshed publication gates, branch push, and one draft PR creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial requests gate implementation; refreshed gates and push/PR calls gate publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run targeted tests before and after the implementation and inspect git diff/stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two targeted test runs plus constant diff inspection per issue, with test count determined by the brief rather than changed-file cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fail-before/pass-after testing and diff validation were already required by the combined skill.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation must complete before maintainer review and publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write a temporary PR body file outside the checkout and pass it to gh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded body file per PR containing the issue brief and summary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old skill passed the same body content inline to gh; the new file adds one small local write while avoiding shell interpolation hazards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A small serialization/write before PR creation; it replaces inline shell argument construction and is not collection-scaled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One issue, one bounded brief, and the files/tests required by that issue; there is no new loop over repository files or issue history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All gates, tests, and publication operations are sequenced; no aggregate burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live issue and PR state is intentionally refreshed before publication. No negative cache or reusable record cache exists, matching the prior workflow.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete old/new command paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test duration depends on the issue's named validation, but the PR does not increase required test multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: direct implement mode removes the prior plan-file creation, while the one PR-body file write is bounded and negligible.

Scenarios.Scenario: Implement a previously created plan-first issue and open a draft PR
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A second skill invocation repeats checkout/auth and live GitHub gates, reads the local plan, then runs implementation/tests, maintainer review, publication gates, push, and PR creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch the Sweeper record, live issue, and open-PR state at implementation handoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One auth check, one record request, one issue request, and one PR search for the implementation invocation; this is a constant extra preflight relative to continuing inside the old combined skill.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old combined skill retained the fetched record and initial gate state while pausing for plan approval, then refreshed issue/PR gates only before shipping; it did not need a second initial record fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a small sequential handoff latency before implementation but ensures the separate invocation sees current readiness, security, issue, and PR state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one local approved plan and later serialize it into one PR body file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded plan read and one bounded PR-body write per issue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The combined skill already retained and read/wrote the plan in the same workflow and embedded it in the PR body, though the body was passed inline rather than via a file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The plan read gates implementation; the body write gates PR creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One issue and one plan file. The repeated preflight remains constant and does not fan out over files, issue comments, records, or changed paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The extra handoff calls are sequential and bounded; no parallel network or subprocess burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The local plan is the persistent handoff state. GitHub state is deliberately not cached across separate invocations; publication gates are refreshed again after review as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the split adds one constant preflight; high confidence that it has no scaling multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency varies, but the added cost is only a fixed handful of requests per plan-first issue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although the split repeats a constant preflight, it is bounded, occurs once per plan-first issue, and intentionally validates authoritative live state at a new invocation boundary rather than creating realistic throughput, memory, or latency harm.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed skill documents and compared each prescribed subprocess, filesystem, test, and GitHub-network boundary with the deleted combined workflow. The split adds only one bounded preflight at the plan-to-implementation handoff and one small PR-body file write; neither creates a realistic scaling or hot-path performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
